stemBlocks.value: Solve the simultaneous equations x + y = 5 and xy = 6.
Think first: One equation is linear and one is not, so substitute from the linear one into the other.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p110-q01 from workbook page 110.

solutionSteps.instruction: Make y the subject of the linear equation.

contentBlocks.value: collect all terms on one side

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the y-value that goes with each x.

strategyBlocks.value: Make y the subject of the linear equation, substitute into xy = 6 to get a quadratic in x, solve it, then find each matching y.

whyThisWorks.value: Substituting the linear equation into the non-linear one reduces two unknowns to one, producing a quadratic whose roots are the possible x-values. Each root must be paired with its own y from the linear equation, since the solutions come in matched pairs rather than as any x with any y. Geometrically you are finding where the straight line x + y = 5 meets the curve xy = 6.

commonErrors.misconception: Listing x = 2, 3 and y = 2, 3 without pairing them up.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Listing x = 2, 3 and y = 2, 3 without pairing them up.

commonErrors.misconception: Substituting into the linear equation, which gives nothing new.

examTip.value: Present non-linear simultaneous answers as ordered pairs so the pairing is unmistakable.
